observation.justification: The common client path: the same search poll every target gets, at the interval frozen for the competitors.

Common-client polling over the captured API's search endpoint (/api/v1/search): a complete scan at once, then one 100 ms after each completed scan, until the cutoff; a match first seen after the cutoff is late (censored). Selected as the labelled common method (proposed decision 0093 §4), not the best available: the reviewed websocket source (sources.lock.json) establishes no lossless wait.

claim.statement: Measures the digest-checked executables named in products, launched with the lock's fixed launch. For an official target each release tag's commit is attributed source context only: nothing ties an executable to it, so no built-from, equivalence or same-build claim is made. Mailpit, MailHog, MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket are official artifacts; GreenMail is an official jar run on a pinned JRE; the alkemio-mailslurper row is a third-party patched image's extracted binary, run natively and never counted as an official competitor row, and the swarmail candidate is neither. MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket tag their releases lightweight, which carries weaker source evidence than an annotated tag. Throughput and observed visibility within the declared deadline are all that is claimed: no durability, no accept==stored and no equivalence. Storage is the unmatched profile and resources the unenforced local profile; both are stated in every report. Targets without a verified server search are scanned completely and filtered on the client, and GreenMail is read over POP3; both are labelled per row.
